title: Re-implement `RBSet` as a subclass of `RBMap` with empty values.

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
Addresses https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/11473 - turns out I did manage to make it work myself after all!

This deduplicates RBTree logic to make the code more maintainable.
Since the code was almost entirely copy-pasted before, the new implementation should behave the same as the old one (I tested this partially below). In particular, it should be (practically) exactly as fast as the previous implementation. `RBMap` functions are not available through `RBSet` since the inheritance is private.

**Note:** The value isn't _entirely_ empty. This appears to be impossible in C++, at least as far as my cursory search went. Instead, the `RBEmptyValue` struct is supposedly compiled as a single char, increasing the memory footprint of every element of `RBSet` by a byte. Considering the size of `RBTree` elements, this should be negligible (and could be mitigated by e.g. changing the `color` property from `int` to `Color`).

## Notes

A few changes had to be made to `RBTree` to avoid interface changes to `RBSet` elements. In particular, `ConstIterator` and `Element` needed to return `keys` instead of `values` or `key-values` for some functions. This was achievable with a template parameter without complex logic.

`RBSet` had a few `const` mistakes.
For one, it was previously possible to non-const iterate its values. Changing the values during iteration would have invalidated the tree. This was luckily not the case in the codebase.
`find_closest` previously returned a non-const `Element` from a `const` function. Now, two versions are offered with correct constness.
Some modules had to be changed throughout the codebase to account for the interface changes, but it wasn't many.
